Adventures in prompt engineering: Claude; research supervisor

Nov 16, 2024

Lately I’ve been interested in learning to get the best out of generative AI tools. I’ve signed up for a subscription to Anthropic’s Claude. These are some of my notes on using it as a tool for my academic writing in an ehtical way.

Many universities seem to have taken the approach to place a blanket ban on generative AI tools like Claude. I think that’s quite stupid.

(more stuff)

Claude projects

### Project level prompt xxx ### Initial project knowledge artifacts xxx ### Closing out a chat thread Claude can't rememeber knowledge across threads, and when a single chat thread becomes too long you consume too many credits plus performance degrades. To avoid those issues, I've decided to break the process up into one thread per chapter / phase of the report writing process. Ideally I don't want to have to try and explain everything that we covered in the previous chat in the first prompt of the new thread. When closing out a thread, I ask Claude to summarize the session and output it as an artifact. I then add this summary document, as well as the draft chapter that resulted from that chat to the project knowledge base. Here is an exmaple of the final prompt for a chat thread: "Please write a summary document that I can hand over to someone so that they understand everything you worked on. Write it in a professional and informative manner and be thorough. Make sure to remove redundancies or old information. The summary document should be a markdown file. OUTPUT AS ARTIFACT." ### Starting a new thread with context from past threads When starting a new thread, the first prompt I give Clause will contain some detailed context on what we will be working in this thread, and what the ideal output at the end of our session will be. Then I ask Claude to read through the summary document and the draft chapter in the knowledge base, referring to them by name.
